Aqueducts. The Romans built monumental water-delivery systems to transport fresh water from distant sources to cities and military camps using gravity and arches rather than pumps. Eleven major aqueducts fed Rome alone, delivering over a million cubic meters of water daily to a city of about a million people. Extended fifty to ninety kilometers from mountain springs with calculated gradients and underground tunnels, they supplied public fountains, bathhouses, and wealthy residences, supporting the reality and mythology of Roman civilization.
